summary:
A trans visitor to Idaho stands under the United States federal framework on documents and entry. Executive Order 14168 of January 2025 requires federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth; the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, new passports are issued only as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already carrying an X remain valid until expiry. The Supreme Court in November 2025 allowed the changed treatment of trans passports to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992, and the ACLU has sued on behalf of seven plaintiffs.

Idaho's own statute is the sharper exposure on the ground. House Bill 752 was signed by the governor and takes effect on 1 July 2026. It makes it a crime for a trans person to use a restroom or changing room not matching birth sex in government buildings and in public-facing private businesses such as gas stations, restaurants, entertainment venues and hospitals. The first offence is a misdemeanour carrying up to a year in jail. The ACLU of Idaho filed suit on 30 April 2026 arguing due-process, equal-protection and privacy violations, noting the law targets no actual criminal conduct. Six transgender Idahoans joined the challenge to block HB 752 before its effect date; the ACLU describes it as the only state law extending bathroom criminalisation to private businesses and as carrying steeper penalties than other states' bans. National wire reporting covered the legislature's passage of the ban and the jail penalties it carries, along with a lawsuit that has partially blocked it.

Entry screening carries its own exposure. The Transportation Security Administration's checkpoint procedures involve secondary screening, hand-held devices and pat-downs that can be invasive of privacy and risk outing a trans traveller.
tangentialFactors:
Idaho's HB 752 sits within a national pattern: state bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and, in some states, government buildings cover 9 states and 1 territory, and some states make trans use of facilities a criminal offence in certain circumstances. In April 2025 a trans student was arrested and handcuffed in a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol after declaring an intention to break the law; civil-rights attorneys described it as the first known arrest under a state bathroom-restriction law.

Idaho is not alone in closing identity documents: in March 2026 Kansas enacted a law invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not match sex assigned at birth, which rights groups call a template for other state legislatures. Gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states; Idaho's own HB 71, signed 4 April 2023, was upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in April 2024.
localsOnly:
Idaho bans any change of sex on birth certificates under a 2018 implementation law allowed into legal effect in January 2026, permitting only biological male or female sex at birth. Since March 2019 Idaho offers an "X" third-gender option on driver's licenses and state IDs, but under an August 7, 2020 ruling applicants changing gender markers must submit a physician letter certifying sex reassignment surgery; in November 2019 the Board of Health and Welfare removed doctor-approval for gender change for transgender minors while retaining parental permission, emancipation, or court order.

Gender-affirming medical care for minors is a felony for doctors under HB 71 signed 4 April 2023, banning puberty blockers, hormones and surgeries. HB 668, effective 1 July 2024, further restricts care for minors and adults when provided by state, local or county professionals, through Idaho Medicaid, or on state property including hospitals, public colleges and prisons, excluding counseling and mental health but limiting HRT and gender-affirming surgery and barring tax deductibility. Transgender prisoners were permitted hormone therapy under a September 2024 federal judge ruling nullifying a 1997 law banning it.

Under a March 2026 law, schools, childcare providers and medical professionals must out transgender minors to parents within three days of learning trans status. An April 2024 law bans teachers and education agencies from using pronouns not based on birth certificates for students. Transgender athletes are barred from public school and university sports teams matching gender identity under legislation signed 30 March 2020. In August 2024 the Governor signed an executive order barring application of any federal laws, regulations and guidelines regarding gender identity or ideology within Idaho.

No Idaho state law explicitly addresses discrimination based on gender identity, but Bostock v. Clayton County (15 June 2020) provides federal Title VII workplace protection, and about 40% of the population is covered by county or city ordinances in Ada County, Bellevue, Boise, Coeur d'Alene, Driggs, Hailey, Idaho Falls, Ketchum, Lewiston, Meridian, Moscow, Pocatello, Sandpoint, Victor plus Latah County employee protection. Idaho's hate-crime law excludes gender identity, but the federal Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Act of October 2009 allows federal prosecution for gender-identity-motivated crimes. Same-sex marriage has been legal since October 2014 following Latta v. Otter.
outOfScopeNotes:
The scope and current enforceability of HB 752 remain unresolved in the sources: one account reports a lawsuit that partially blocked the law, while another reports a 16 June 2026 narrowing by U.S. District Judge Amanda Brailsford barring enforcement against single-stall use or multi-user use when no unoccupied single-user restroom is on the same floor. Whether the 1 July 2026 effective date holds, and whether the felony or misdemeanour penalty classification controls, is not resolved in the inventory.

The inventory does not document any Idaho-specific airport screening incident involving a trans traveller; the TSA screening exposure cited is national, not Idaho-specific. Whether the federal passport litigation will alter the current document position before or during travel is not sourced and should be checked before departure.
